name: What is the difference between resurfacing and replacing a pool deck?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between resurfacing and replacing a pool deck?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resurfacing involves applying a new layer or coating over the existing pool deck, often used to cover minor cracks, stains, or update its appearance without full demolition. This is typically a more cost-effective and quicker option. Replacing a pool deck involves complete demolition and removal of the old deck, followed by the installation of a brand-new one. Replacement is necessary when the existing deck has significant structural damage, extensive cracking, or if you desire a completely different material or layout that cannot be achieved through resurfacing.
acceptedAnswer.description: Resurfacing adds a new layer over an existing deck for cosmetic fixes, while replacing involves full demolition and new installation for significant damage or major design changes.
